title.zh: 卷457 列傳二百四十四 蒋东才 刘廷 李承先 李南华兄：子得胜 董履高 董全胜 牛师韩 曹德庆 马復震 程文炳 方耀 郑绍忠 邓安邦
title.en: Volume 457 Biographies 244: Jiang Dongcai, Liu Ting, Li Chengxian, Li Nanhua Elder Brother: Zi De Sheng, Dong Lvgao, Dong Quansheng, Niu Shihan, Cao Deqing, Ma Fuzhen, Cheng Wenbing, Fang Yao, Zheng Shaozhong, Deng Anbang
title.raw: 卷457 列傳二百四十四 蒋东才 刘廷 李承先 李南华兄：子得胜 董履高 董全胜 牛师韩 曹德庆 马復震 程文炳 方耀 郑绍忠 邓安邦

sentences.zh: 蔣東才，字軼眾，安徽亳州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Dongcai, courtesy name Yizhong, was a man of Bozhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dongcai, styled Yizhong, was a native of Bozhou, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，捻酋張洛行圍城，築砲台高阜，俯擊城中，東才兄遇害，憤甚，乃創義團，為官軍前驅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, the Nian chieftain Zhang Luoxing besieged the city, built gun platforms on high ground to strike down into the city; Dongcai's elder brother met harm, and in great anger he then founded a righteous militia as vanguard for the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign, the Nian chieftain Zhang Luoxing besieged the city and built gun emplacements on high ground to rain fire down on it. Dongcai's elder brother was killed in the fighting; enraged, he raised a volunteer militia to serve as vanguard for government troops.

sentences.zh: 會城中糧盡，東才殺馬饗士，與同邑劉廷、李承先夜縋城出襲，毀之，寇遁。

translations.literal: When provisions in the city were exhausted, Dongcai killed horses to feast the troops; with fellow-townsmen Liu Ting and Li Chengxian he was lowered from the wall by night to strike out, destroyed them, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the city's grain ran out, Dongcai slaughtered horses to feed his men. With fellow townsman Liu Ting and Li Chengxian, he let himself down from the walls by night to storm the emplacements, destroyed them, and the raiders fled.

sentences.zh: 四年，投豫軍，英翰器其才，俾充哨長。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he joined the Henan army; Ying Han valued his talent and had him serve as squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1854) he enlisted in the Henan army. Ying Han recognized his ability and appointed him squad leader.

sentences.zh: 戰亳北，被巨創，卒擒其渠。

translations.literal: Fighting north of Bozhou he received a great wound, but in the end captured their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In battle north of Bozhou he suffered grave wounds but finally captured the rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 南道團練大臣毛昶熙檄領東震營，累勳至守備。

translations.literal: Mao Changxi, minister of southern-route militia training, ordered him to command the Dongzhen battalion; through accumulated merit he reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Changxi, the southern-route militia minister, appointed him to command the Dongzhen Battalion, and through repeated merit he rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 商丘寇之據金樓也，東才築土為山頓其上。

translations.literal: When bandits at Shangqiu held Jinlou, Dongcai piled earth into a mountain and encamped atop it.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels held Jinlou near Shangqiu, Dongcai heaped earth into a mound and stationed his troops on top.

sentences.zh: 寇來襲，輒敗去，縱兵乘之，遇伏，砲石雨坌。

translations.literal: When bandits came to attack they were always beaten and withdrew; he sent troops in pursuit, met an ambush, and cannon stones rained down in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels attacked they were driven back; he sent men in pursuit but ran into an ambush, and cannonballs and stones poured down like rain.

sentences.zh: 東才方解衣激戰，寇突出襲我後，東才回矛決盪，大殲其眾，寨拔。

translations.literal: Dongcai had just stripped for fierce fighting when bandits suddenly burst out to strike our rear; Dongcai wheeled his spear and swept through, greatly slaughtering their host, and the stockade was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Dongcai had stripped for close combat when the enemy suddenly struck from the rear. He wheeled about with his spear, cut through their ranks, slaughtered the main force, and captured the stockade.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，規汝寧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, they planned to take Runing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi (1863) they set out to capture Runing.

sentences.zh: 夜獲邏卒，東才乃服寇裝，效口號，奪門入，諸軍踵之，夷巨壘。

translations.literal: By night they captured a courier; Dongcai then wore bandit dress, imitated their passwords, seized the gate and entered, the armies followed, and the great fortress was razed.
translations.idiomatic: By night they captured a courier. Dongcai donned rebel garb, mimicked their watchwords, seized the gate, and led the main force in behind him; the great fortress was leveled.

sentences.zh: 乘勢下南陽、息縣，又敗之商丘大周集。

translations.literal: Riding the momentum they took Nanyang and Xixian, and again defeated them at Dazhouji in Shangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage they took Nanyang and Xixian, and again routed the enemy at Dazhouji near Shangqiu.

sentences.zh: 數遷至副將。

translations.literal: Through several promotions he reached vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he attained the rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，張總愚北犯，東才攻以火，殪寇千餘。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Zhang Zongyu invaded north; Dongcai attacked with fire and destroyed more than a thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1868) Zhang Zongyu pushed north; Dongcai assailed them with fire and killed more than a thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 又截擊任柱等黃河、徒駭間，晉總兵，賜號威勇巴圖魯，徙守運河。

translations.literal: He again intercepted Ren Zhu and others between the Yellow River and the Tuhai, was promoted to major-general, granted the title Valiant and Brave Batulu, and transferred to guard the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He also intercepted Ren Zhu and others between the Yellow River and the Tuhai, was promoted to major-general, granted the title "Valiant and Brave Batulu," and transferred to guard the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 捻平，擢提督。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified, he was elevated to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian rebellion was suppressed, he was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 明年，赴陝徵甘肅竄匪，並敗退波羅營以西馬賊，更勇號額騰額。

translations.literal: The next year he went to Shaanxi to campaign against Gansu marauding bandits, and together defeated and drove back Muslim rebels west of Boluo camp; he received a further brave title, Eteng'e.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went to Shaanxi to suppress Gansu raiders, defeated the Muslim rebels west of Boluo camp, and was granted a further brave title, Eteng'e.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從克肅州，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed in the capture of Suzhou and was rewarded with a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he took part in the capture of Suzhou (Jiuquan) and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 事寧，假歸。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he took leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，統領豫軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he commanded the Henan army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign he took command of the Henan army.

sentences.zh: 先後疏浚賈魯河、京師內外城河。

translations.literal: He successively dredged the Jialu River and the inner and outer moat rivers of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He successively dredged the Jialu River and the inner and outer moats of the capital.

sentences.zh: 除甘肅涼州鎮總兵，仍留豫。

translations.literal: He was appointed major-general of Liangzhou garrison in Gansu but remained in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed major-general of the Liangzhou garrison in Gansu but continued to serve in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，黃水暴漲，力護鄭州以下堤工，救難民二千餘。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Yellow River rose violently; he strove to protect the dikes below Zhengzhou and rescued more than two thousand disaster victims.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1887) the Yellow River surged; he threw himself into protecting the dikes below Zhengzhou and rescued more than two thousand flood victims.

sentences.zh: 風雨罷勞，遘疾困篤，俄卒於工次。

translations.literal: Wind and rain without cease from labor, he fell gravely ill and soon died at his post on the works.
translations.idiomatic: Worn out by wind and rain and unceasing labor, he fell gravely ill and soon died at his post on the river works.

sentences.zh: 優詔賜卹，予開封、亳州建祠。

translations.literal: An excellent edict granted mourning favors and ordered temples built in Kaifeng and Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict granted posthumous honors and authorized temples in his memory at Kaifeng and Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 廷既解亳圍，旋奪西境兩河口，補千總，從宋慶駐守宋集。

translations.literal: After Ting had relieved the Bozhou siege, he soon retook the Two River Mouths on the western border, was made warrant officer, and followed Song Qing in garrison at Songji.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ting had lifted the siege of Bozhou, he soon recaptured the Two River Mouths on the western frontier, was appointed warrant officer, and joined Song Qing in garrison at Songji.

sentences.zh: 同治間，從攻懷遠，平高丘，積功至參將。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi he followed attacks on Huaiyuan, pacified Gaoqiu, and through accumulated merit reached colonel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi years he took part in the assault on Huaiyuan and the pacification of Gaoqiu, rising through merit to colonel.

sentences.zh: 任柱等掘滎澤將圖北，又從慶迎擊。

translations.literal: Ren Zhu and others were digging the Ying marsh intending to move north; he again followed Qing to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Zhu and others were digging the Ying marsh with plans to push north, he again followed Song Qing to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 夜率壯士襲其營，寇南走，廷截之光州，誅其酋張顯。

translations.literal: By night he led stalwarts in a surprise on their camp; the bandits fled south, and Ting intercepted them at Guangzhou and executed their chieftain Zhang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: By night he led picked men in a raid on their camp. The rebels fled south; Ting cut them off at Guangzhou and executed their leader Zhang Xian.

sentences.zh: 复破張總愚於饒陽、臨邑，擢總兵。

translations.literal: He again defeated Zhang Zongyu at Raoyang and Linyi and was promoted to major-general.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Zhang Zongyu at Raoyang and Linyi and was promoted to major-general.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，晉提督，賜號額騰依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified he was advanced to provincial military commander and granted the title Etengyi Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were suppressed he was promoted to provincial military commander and granted the title Etengyi Batulu.

sentences.zh: 八年，入陝平綏德，賜秩頭品。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered Shaanxi and pacified Suide, and was given rank of first-grade button.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he entered Shaanxi, pacified Suide, and was awarded first-grade court rank.

sentences.zh: 寧夏既寧，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: After Ningxia was pacified he was rewarded with a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ningxia was pacified he was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒於洛陽，祀亳州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died at Luoyang; a shrine was established in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu (1878) he died at Luoyang; a memorial shrine was erected in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 承先，字光前。

translations.literal: Chengxian, courtesy name Guangqian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengxian, styled Guangqian.

sentences.zh: 少英敏，好讀明戚繼光書。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and clever, fond of reading the Ming dynasty works of Qi Jiguang.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and devoted to reading the military writings of the Ming general Qi Jiguang.

sentences.zh: 亳平，赴歸德擊高州匪，拔汝寧寨，與有功。

translations.literal: After Bozhou was pacified he went to Guide to strike Gaozhou bandits, captured the Runing stockade, and shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Bozhou was pacified he marched to Guide to fight Gaozhou rebels, captured the Runing stockade, and earned a share of the credit.

sentences.zh: 同治間，攻張岡，匪首孫葵心來援，圍承先數匝，冒圍出，裹創力戰，敗之，遷都司。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi, attacking Zhanggang, bandit chief Sun Kuixin came to reinforce; they surrounded Chengxian many rings deep; he broke through the encirclement, fought on wrapped in wounds, defeated them, and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongzhi, while attacking Zhanggang, the bandit chief Sun Kuixin came to relieve the place and surrounded Chengxian in many rings. He broke out of the encirclement, fought on despite his wounds, routed the enemy, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 進解光州圍，連敗之上蔡、祥符。

translations.literal: Advancing he relieved the siege of Guangzhou and won successive victories at Shangcai and Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward he lifted the siege of Guangzhou and won successive victories at Shangcai and Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 守黃河，降中牟寇馮增，再遷副將。

translations.literal: Guarding the Yellow River he induced the Zhongmu bandit Feng Zeng to surrender and was again promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: While guarding the Yellow River he induced the Zhongmu rebel Feng Zeng to surrender and was again promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 張總愚竄畿南，又從慶敗之饒陽，賜號節勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region; again following Qing he defeated him at Raoyang and was granted the title Jieyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region, he again followed Song Qing and defeated him at Raoyang, receiving the title Jieyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 長驅玉林鎮，戰良久，中矛，浴血陷陣，大捷。

translations.literal: Making a long drive to Yulin town he fought for a long time, was struck by a spear, bathed in blood plunged into the formation, and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He drove hard to Yulin town, fought for hours, took a spear wound, and plunged into the fray drenched in blood, winning a great victory.

sentences.zh: 逐北濟陽，直蹙之黃河，晉號志勇，擢總兵。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Jiyang he pressed them straight to the Yellow River, was advanced to the title Zhiyong, and promoted to major-general.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the enemy north to Jiyang, he pressed them to the Yellow River, was granted the title Zhiyong, and promoted to major-general.

sentences.zh: 錄守運河功，晉提督。

translations.literal: Recording merit for guarding the canal he was advanced to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service guarding the Grand Canal he was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，河工成，遣散夫役近數万，為奸民所惑，嘯聚硃仙鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu, when river works were completed, nearly tens of thousands of laborers were dismissed; deluded by troublemakers they gathered clamoring at Zhuxian town.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu (1888), when the river works were finished, nearly ten thousand laborers were dismissed. Misled by agitators, they gathered in a clamor at Zhuxian town.

sentences.zh: 提督董明禮被圍，巡撫倪文蔚議剿，承先止之曰：「用兵必有潰擾，歸、陳各屬不能安枕矣！

translations.literal: Provincial commander Dong Mingli was besieged; Governor Ni Wenwei planned suppression; Chengxian stopped him saying: 'Using troops will certainly cause rout and disturbance—the prefectures of Guide and Chen cannot rest easy!
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commander Dong Mingli was besieged. Governor Ni Wenwei proposed a punitive campaign, but Chengxian dissuaded him, saying: "If we send troops there will surely be rout and disorder—the prefectures of Guide and Chen will not be able to sleep in peace!

sentences.zh: 且河工夫役數十萬，設有牽動，患更大。」

translations.literal: Moreover there are hundreds of thousands on river works; if they are stirred up the calamity will be greater.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, there are hundreds of thousands of men on the river works; if they are drawn into this, the harm will be far greater."

sentences.zh: 乃單騎往撫，杖其前者數人，餘皆愕錯，受部勒。

translations.literal: He then went alone on horseback to pacify them, clubbed several of those in front, the rest were startled and confused and submitted to discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode out alone to pacify them, clubbed several of the ringleaders, and the rest, stunned, submitted to his orders.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署河北鎮總兵，自同治八年至是凡三攝矣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he acted as major-general of Hebei garrison; from the eighth year of Tongzhi to then he had held acting posts three times.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he served as acting major-general of the Hebei garrison; from the eighth year of Tongzhi to that time he had held acting command three times.

sentences.zh: 尋補歸德鎮。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed to Guide garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed permanent commander of the Guide garrison.

sentences.zh: 四月，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he died.

sentences.zh: 亳民感之，建祠以祀。

translations.literal: The people of Bozhou were grateful and built a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Bozhou, moved by his deeds, built a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 李南華，字孟莊，安徽蒙城人。

translations.literal: Li Nanhua, courtesy name Mengzhuang, was a man of Mengcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nanhua, styled Mengzhuang, was a native of Mengcheng, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，粵寇陷江寧，淮北捻蜂起。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng the Taiping rebels took Jiangning; Nian rebels rose in swarms in north Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign the Taiping rebels seized Nanjing, and Nian rebels swarmed across north Huai.

sentences.zh: 南華治團衛鄉里，擊捻數獲勝，累勳至守備。

translations.literal: Nanhua organized militia to defend the countryside, struck the Nian many times with victory, and through accumulated merit reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhua organized militia to defend his district, fought the Nian repeatedly with success, and through accumulated merit rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 捻入境，率死士百人拒之，斬悍賊百餘，進討群捻，七戰皆捷，遷游擊，賜號猛勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When Nian entered the territory he led a hundred men willing to die to resist them, beheaded more than a hundred fierce bandits, advanced to subdue grouped Nian with seven battles all victorious, was promoted to raiding commander, granted title Mengyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian crossed the border he led a hundred men willing to die in his defense, cut down more than a hundred of their fiercest fighters, marched against the main Nian bands with seven straight victories, was promoted to raiding commander, and granted the title Mengyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，平澮北。

translations.literal: At the change to Tongzhi he pacified north Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongzhi reign began he pacified the country north of the Sui River.

sentences.zh: 先是，苗練沛霖跨有長淮，既輸款發、捻，大誅練之異己者，群練帖伏。

translations.literal: Previously Miao militia trainer Pei Lin had spanned the Long Huai; after he submitted tribute to the Taiping and Nian he massacred militia who disagreed with him, and the militia groups submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Miao militia leader Miao Peilin had dominated the Huai River region. After he made terms with the Taiping and Nian, he slaughtered militia who opposed him, and the other militia bands submitted.

sentences.zh: 獨南華與抗，翦除其黨，沛霖怒，遣張建猷等圍蒙。

translations.literal: Only Nanhua resisted, eliminated his faction; Pei Lin was enraged and sent Zhang Jianyou and others to besiege Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhua alone held out against him and destroyed his partisans. Enraged, Peilin sent Zhang Jianyou and others to besiege Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 南華破之馬家店，再至再敗之，尋就撫。

translations.literal: Nanhua defeated them at Majiadian, defeated them again when they returned, and soon submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhua routed them at Majiadian and defeated them again when they returned; Peilin soon submitted to pacification.

sentences.zh: 明年，复叛，築壘蒙城東南，斷我糧運，南華會總兵王才秀擊卻之。

translations.literal: The next year he rebelled again, built fortresses southeast of Mengcheng, cut off our grain transport; Nanhua joined major-general Wang Caixiu to attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Peilin rebelled again, built fortresses southeast of Mengcheng, and cut government grain routes. Nanhua joined major-general Wang Caixiu in driving them back.

sentences.zh: 沛霖深塹長濠，謀久困。

translations.literal: Pei Lin dug deep trenches and long moats planning to wear them down over time.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin dug deep trenches and long moats, intending to wear the city down through a prolonged siege.

sentences.zh: 南華誓死守，數出戰，負重創，力疾攻之，屍山積。

translations.literal: Nanhua swore to defend to the death, sallied many times, bore grave wounds, attacked vigorously despite illness, corpses piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhua swore to hold the city to the death, led repeated sorties despite grave wounds, and pressed the attack even while ill until corpses piled like hills.

sentences.zh: 會糧絕，令眾潛取之以為食，一夕皆盡，寇大駴。

translations.literal: When provisions ran out he had the troops secretly take enemy bodies for food; in one night they were all consumed and the bandits were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When grain ran out he had his men secretly take corpses from the enemy lines for food; in a single night they were all consumed, and the besiegers were thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 出奇兵夜襲之，奪其輜重以歸，斬馘不可稱計。

translations.literal: He sent elite troops in a night raid, seized their baggage wagons to return, and beheaded the enemy beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He sent elite troops in a night raid, carried off their baggage train, and killed the enemy in numbers beyond count.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁入城，見家食人肉，南華竟體創痕，深嘆異之。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen entered the city and saw families eating human flesh; Nanhua's whole body bore wound marks—he sighed in deep wonder.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengge Rinchen entered the city he found families eating human flesh. Nanhua's body was covered with wounds, and the prince marveled deeply.

sentences.zh: 唐訓方上其功，超擢總兵。

translations.literal: Tang Xunfang reported his merit and he was leap-promoted to major-general.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xunfang memorialized his achievements, and he was promoted by special leap to major-general.

sentences.zh: 未幾，統全軍駐守懷遠。

translations.literal: Before long he commanded the entire army garrisoning Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took command of the full force garrisoning Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙臨淮、壽州。

translations.literal: In the third year he transferred to Linhuai and Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to garrison Linhuai and Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞任柱入蒙境，亟還軍，而捻又竄豫，巡撫喬松年移撫陝，奏自隨。

translations.literal: Hearing Ren Zhu had entered Meng territory he hurried back with the army, but the Nian again fled into Henan; Governor Qiao Songnian was transferred to Shaanxi and memorialized that Nanhua should accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Ren Zhu had entered Meng territory, he hurried back with his troops, but the Nian again fled into Henan. When Governor Qiao Songnian was transferred to Shaanxi, he memorialized that Nanhua should accompany him.

sentences.zh: 張總愚擾關中，率師馳擊之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu harassed Guanzhong; he led troops in swift pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zongyu harassed Guanzhong he led his troops in swift pursuit.

sentences.zh: 陝事定，稱疾去。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi affairs were settled he claimed illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs in Shaanxi were settled he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 久家居，慷慨好義，值歲饑嗛，毀家紓難，誦聲如沸焉。

translations.literal: Long living at home, generous and fond of righteousness, when famine came he ruined his estate to relieve distress and praise for him boiled like surf.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for many years, generous and public-spirited. In years of famine he spent his fortune to relieve distress, and praise for him spread like boiling water.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，土寇牛世修倡亂渦陽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu local bandit Niu Shixiu incited rebellion at Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu (1898) the local bandit Niu Shixiu incited rebellion at Guoyang.

sentences.zh: 南華聞警，率練勇赴援，會各軍擊退之。

translations.literal: Nanhua heard the alarm and led militia to aid; the various armies joined to beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Nanhua led militia to the rescue, and together with the regular forces drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 明年，巡撫鄧華熙疏薦其才，令綜鳳、潁、六、泗團練，參皖北軍事。

translations.literal: The next year Governor Deng Huaxi memorialized recommending his talent, ordering him to oversee Fengyang, Yingzhou, Lu'an, and Sizhou militia and participate in north Anhui military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Governor Deng Huaxi memorialized recommending his ability and placed him in charge of militia in Fengyang, Yingzhou, Lu'an, and Sizhou, with a role in north Anhui military affairs.

sentences.zh: 數獲劇盜，萑蒲斂跡。

translations.literal: He captured many major bandits and lawless elements fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He captured many notorious bandits, and lawlessness in the region subsided.

sentences.zh: 調赴豫，權河北鎮總兵，尋補福建汀州鎮。

translations.literal: Transferred to Henan, acted as Hebei garrison major-general, soon appointed Fujian Tingzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Henan, served as acting major-general of the Hebei garrison, and was soon appointed to the Tingzhou garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died.

sentences.zh: 鄉人思其德，籥建蒙城專祠，報可。

translations.literal: Fellow townspeople mindful of his virtue petitioned to build a dedicated temple in Mengcheng; approved.
translations.idiomatic: His countrymen, mindful of his virtue, petitioned to build a dedicated shrine in Mengcheng; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 其兄子得勝，佐治鄉團，亦頗力。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Desheng assisted in managing district militia and also exerted himself greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Zi Desheng helped manage the local militia and also served with considerable energy.

sentences.zh: 沛霖之亂，戰常陷堅。

translations.literal: During Pei Lin's rebellion he often fought in the fiercest places.
translations.idiomatic: During Peilin's rebellion he repeatedly fought in the thickest of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 累遷參將，賜號奮勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached colonel and was granted the title Fenyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to colonel and was granted the title Fenyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 蒙圍解，改練為軍，俾得勝領之。

translations.literal: When the Meng siege was lifted the militia was converted to regular troops and Desheng was made to command them.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege of Mengcheng was lifted, the militia was reorganized as regular troops under Desheng's command.

sentences.zh: 轉戰直、魯、蘇、豫，頗有功。

translations.literal: Campaigning through Zhili, Shandong, Jiangsu, and Henan he achieved considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned across Zhili, Shandong, Jiangsu, and Henan and won considerable distinction.

sentences.zh: 克宿遷、郯城，擢總兵，補安慶協副將。

translations.literal: Capturing Suqian and Tancheng he was promoted major-general and appointed Anqing assistant vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Suqian and Tancheng he was promoted to major-general and appointed assistant vice commander of the Anqing garrison.

sentences.zh: 直、東平，晉提督，更勇號曰剛安。

translations.literal: When Zhili and the east were pacified he was advanced to provincial military commander with a further brave title Gang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhili and the east were pacified he was promoted to provincial military commander and granted a further brave title, Gang'an.

sentences.zh: 移軍江寧，平土寇胡志瑞亂，仍歸於亳。

translations.literal: Moving troops to Jiangning he pacified the local bandit Huo Zhihui rebellion and returned to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his troops to Jiangning, suppressed the local bandit Huo Zhihui's rebellion, and returned to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，卹如製，附祀英翰祠。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; mourning per regulations, attached worship at Ying Han's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died; posthumous honors followed regulations, and he was granted attached worship at Ying Han's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 董履高，字仰之，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Dong Lügao, courtesy name Yangzhi, was a man of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Lügao, styled Yangzhi, was a native of Hefei, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐末，粵寇亂，治練衛鄉里。

translations.literal: Late in Xianfeng when Taiping rebels caused turmoil he organized militia to defend the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianfeng reign, when the Taiping rebellion spread, he organized militia to defend his district.

sentences.zh: 同治元年春，李鴻章治軍上海，履高隸戲下，從援北新涇、四江口。

translations.literal: In the first spring month of Tongzhi's first year Li Hongzhang assembled an army at Shanghai; Lügao served under him and followed relief of Beixinjing and Sikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Tongzhi (1862) Li Hongzhang raised an army at Shanghai. Lügao served under him and took part in relieving Beixinjing and Sikou.

sentences.zh: 師攻常熟弗克，履高率敢死士數百先登，拔之。

translations.literal: When the army attacked Changshu without success Lügao led several hundred dare-to-die men to scale first and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army failed to take Changshu, Lügao led several hundred volunteers up the walls first and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 連克昭文。

translations.literal: In succession he captured Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Zhaowen in succession.

sentences.zh: 歷遷至守備。

translations.literal: Through promotions he reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 二年，從克江陰、無錫、金匱，移師浙江。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed in the capture of Jiangyin, Wuxi, and Jinkui; the army moved to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he helped capture Jiangyin, Wuxi, and Jinkui, and the army shifted operations to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時寇麕集嘉善，江、浙道梗。

translations.literal: At the time bandits had massed at Jiashan and Jiangsu-Zhejiang communications were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had massed at Jiashan, and communications between Jiangsu and Zhejiang were cut.

sentences.zh: 西塘勢險奧，寇據為嘉善犄角，殊死眾。

translations.literal: Xitang's terrain was steep and hidden; bandits held it as Jiashan's horn position, fighting to the death in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Xitang was rugged and defensible; the rebels held it as an outwork of Jiashan and fought there with desperate numbers.

sentences.zh: 履高率眾泅濟，直薄壘下，砲彈掠肩過，弗少顧，譟而上，手刃數悍賊，奪纛而舞，氣百倍，寇驚亂，拔西塘。

translations.literal: Lügao led troops swimming across, pressed straight under the ramparts; cannonballs skimmed past his shoulders but he did not glance aside; shouting they climbed up, personally killed several fierce bandits, seized banners and danced them, morale a hundredfold; bandits panicked and Xitang was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Lügao led his men swimming the river and pressed straight to the ramparts. Cannonballs skimmed past his shoulders, but he never flinched. With a shout his men scaled the walls; he personally killed several fierce rebels, seized an enemy banner and waved it aloft, and morale surged a hundredfold. The enemy panicked, and Xitang fell.

sentences.zh: 旋克嘉善，江、浙師始相應。

translations.literal: Soon Jiashan was captured and Jiangsu-Zhejiang forces could finally coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashan was soon taken, and the Jiangsu and Zhejiang columns could at last coordinate.

sentences.zh: 四年，師复宜興、荊溪、嘉定、溧陽，履高每戰必克。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the army again took Yixing, Jingxi, Jiading, and Liyang; Lügao captured every place he fought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the army recaptured Yixing, Jingxi, Jiading, and Liyang; Lügao won every battle he fought.

sentences.zh: 追擊金壇寇，斬馘數千，餘黨星散。

translations.literal: Pursuing bandits at Jintan he beheaded thousands; the remainder scattered like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the rebels at Jintan he killed thousands; the survivors scattered in all directions.

sentences.zh: 五年，援湖州，破廣德，晉游擊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he relieved Huzhou, took Guangde, and was promoted to raiding commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he relieved Huzhou, captured Guangde, and was promoted to raiding commander.

sentences.zh: 鴻章徵捻，檄履高出淮城，次車橋鎮，遇寇，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang campaigned against the Nian he ordered Lügao out from Huai city, encamped at Cheqiao town, met bandits, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang marched against the Nian he summoned Lügao from Huai'an, encamped at Cheqiao, met the enemy, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 寇截淮關稅銀，一日夜馳數百里奪還。

translations.literal: Bandits intercepted Huai customs silver; in one day and night he galloped several hundred li and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized customs silver at the Huai tax station, he rode several hundred li in a single day and night to recover it.

sentences.zh: 時捻酋張總愚竄陝西，任柱、賴文光竄山東，履高東西馳逐，夷阬谷，拔鹵莽，當者輒靡。

translations.literal: At the time Nian chieftain Zhang Zongyu had fled to Shaanxi while Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang were in Shandong; Lügao chased east and west, leveled ravines and gullies, seized strongholds in the wilds, and all who faced him were crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyu had fled into Shaanxi while Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang were in Shandong. Lügao ranged east and west, stormed ravines and wild strongholds, and swept aside all who stood before him.

sentences.zh: 捻集麻城、光山、固始間，編木為城，實土其中，燃砲俯擊，眾莫敢偪。

translations.literal: The Nian gathered between Macheng, Guangshan, and Gushi, weaving wood into walls and packing earth within, firing cannon down on attackers; none dared press close.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian massed between Macheng, Guangshan, and Gushi, building wooden walls packed with earth and firing down on assailants; no one dared approach.

sentences.zh: 履高率千人，夜掘隧，曳木入，衷擊之，盡殪，擢副將。

translations.literal: Lügao led a thousand men, dug tunnels by night, dragged the wooden walls inward, and struck from within; all were destroyed and he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Lügao led a thousand men, tunneled under the walls by night, pulled the wooden defenses inward, and attacked from inside; the enemy was annihilated and he was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 事寧，假歸省親。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he took leave to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he took leave to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 九年，募淮軍赴晉防河，以功晉總兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he recruited Huai army troops to go to Shanxi to guard the river and through merit was promoted to major-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he raised Huai troops for river defense in Shanxi and was promoted to major-general for his service.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，蒙古草地馬賊蜂起，移師防歸化、包頭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu Muslim horse bandits rose on the Mongolian grasslands; he moved troops to defend Guihua and Baotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu horse bandits swarmed the Mongolian steppe; he shifted his forces to defend Guihua and Baotou.

sentences.zh: 沙漠平衍，寇騎梠疾，日嘗數遇，以寡擊眾，月餘，討平之。

translations.literal: The desert was flat and open; bandit cavalry were swift and they met several times a day; with few he struck many, and in little more than a month he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The desert was open country and the raiders' horses were fast; they clashed several times a day. Fighting against odds for over a month, he suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 母憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 五年，起署潯州協副將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled to act as assistant vice commander of the Xunzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to serve as acting assistant vice commander at Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 鬱林大竹根故盜藪，官軍莫能製。

translations.literal: Dazhugen in Yulin was an old bandit lair that government troops could not control.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhugen in Yulin was a longtime bandit stronghold that government troops had been unable to subdue.

sentences.zh: 履高至，潛易裝诇其地，選勁卒數百，距寇巢十里外而軍，佯示怯，寇易之，不戒備。

translations.literal: When Lügao arrived he secretly changed dress to scout the ground, selected several hundred stalwarts, encamped ten li from the bandit nest, and feigned timidity so the bandits despised him and were unguarded.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he disguised himself to reconnoiter the terrain, chose several hundred picked men, and encamped ten li from the bandit lair, feigning timidity so the enemy grew careless.

sentences.zh: 忽大風雨，履高銳師宵加之，擊殺數百人，寇奔遁。

translations.literal: Suddenly in great wind and rain Lügao's elite troops attacked by night, killing several hundred; the bandits fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden storm broke; Lügao sent his best troops in a night attack, killed several hundred, and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 九年，法越肇釁，移頓南寧、龍州備策應。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Franco-Vietnamese conflict began; he moved to garrison Nanning and Longzhou to stand ready.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year war broke out between France and Vietnam; he moved to Nanning and Longzhou to prepare.

sentences.zh: 明年，再署潯州協。

translations.literal: The next year he again acted at the Xunzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again held acting command at Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 思恩革生莫夢弼構苗匪，廣、黔各匪，據五崗以叛。

translations.literal: In Si'en the native Mo Mengbi stirred Miao bandits; Guangxi and Guizhou bandits of every sort held Wugang in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Si'en the native official Mo Mengbi incited Miao rebels; bandits from Guangxi and Guizhou seized Wugang in revolt.

sentences.zh: 五月，深入苗疆，擒夢弼誅之，事遂定。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he penetrated deep into the Miao country, captured Mengbi and executed him, and affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he penetrated deep into Miao territory, captured Mengbi and executed him, and the disturbance was ended.

sentences.zh: 擢提督，賜號奇車伯巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was elevated to provincial military commander and granted the title Qichebo Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial military commander and granted the title Qichebo Batulu.

sentences.zh: 調署新太協，仍駐龍州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to act at the Xintai garrison while still stationed at Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act at the Xintai garrison while remaining at Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，徙屯枚，與法軍血戰數晝夜，左足中砲幾斷，當軸遽易之，諒山遂陷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he moved to garrison Mei and fought the French army in bloody battle for several days and nights; his left foot was nearly severed by cannon; the court leadership hastily replaced him and Lang Son then fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he encamped at Mei and fought the French for several days and nights. A cannonball nearly severed his left foot; the high command hastily replaced him, and Lang Son then fell.

sentences.zh: 年餘，創平，除慶遠協。

translations.literal: After more than a year his wounds healed and he was appointed to the Qingyuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year his wounds healed and he was appointed to the Qingyuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋謝病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十五年，補廣西左江鎮總兵，嚴軍紀，能捕劇盜，鄉民感之，為立主生祀焉。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed major-general of the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi; he enforced strict discipline, could capture major bandits, and the people were grateful and established living worship for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed major-general of the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi. He enforced strict discipline, captured notorious bandits, and the people were so grateful they established living worship in his honor.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調直隸正定。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Zhengding in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Zhengding in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時拳民始萌蘗，月朔望說法愚民。

translations.literal: At the time the Boxers were just sprouting; on the first and fifteenth of each month they preached doctrines to deceive the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxer movement was just emerging; on the first and fifteenth of each month they preached to delude the common people.

sentences.zh: 履高督兵擒其渠，繩以法，餘皆股栗，匪卒不敢入境。

translations.literal: Lügao supervised troops in seizing their leaders and punishing them by law; the rest trembled and the bandits dared not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Lügao had his troops seize the ringleaders and punish them by law; the rest trembled, and the Boxers dared not enter his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 明年，畿輔大亂，獨正定晏然。

translations.literal: The next year the capital region fell into great disorder, but Zhengding alone remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the capital region erupted in chaos, yet Zhengding alone remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 歷江蘇淮揚鎮、貴州安義鎮，袁世凱疏留北洋練軍。

translations.literal: He served at the Huai-Yang garrison in Jiangsu and the Anyi garrison in Guizhou; Yuan Shikai memorialized to retain him with the Beiyang training army.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Huai-Yang garrison in Jiangsu and the Anyi garrison in Guizhou; Yuan Shikai memorialized to keep him with the Beiyang training forces.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，除壽春鎮。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was appointed to the Shouchun garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was appointed commander of the Shouchun garrison.

sentences.zh: 淮流盛漲，城不沒者數尺。

translations.literal: The Huai River rose violently; the city was submerged to within several chi of the top.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai surged; the floodwaters reached to within several feet of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 履高晨夜徼循，修補救護，城得無虞。

translations.literal: Lügao patrolled day and night, repaired and protected the works, and the city escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Lügao patrolled day and night, repaired and reinforced the defenses, and the city was spared.

sentences.zh: 三十二年冬，巡視泗州防營，墜馬，舊創發，假歸。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirty-second year while inspecting the Sizhou defense camp he fell from his horse; old wounds reopened and he took leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirty-second year, while inspecting the Sizhou garrison, he fell from his horse; old wounds reopened and he took leave.

sentences.zh: 越二年，卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 詔優恤，予建祠。

translations.literal: An edict granted generous mourning favors and ordered a memorial temple built.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict granted generous posthumous honors and authorized a memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 董全勝，字凱臣，江蘇銅山人。

translations.literal: Dong Quansheng, courtesy name Kaichen, was a man of Tongshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Quansheng, styled Kaichen, was a native of Tongshan, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 同治初，以把總隸李鴻章軍，充馬隊官。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi as warrant officer he served in Li Hongzhang's army as cavalry officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he served as warrant officer in Li Hongzhang's army and was made cavalry officer.

sentences.zh: 攻無錫，全勝率敢死士為軍先，擒偽潮王黃子隆，城遂克。

translations.literal: Attacking Wuxi, Quansheng led dare-to-die men as army vanguard, captured the false Chaowang Huang Zilong, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Wuxi, Quansheng led volunteers at the head of the column, captured the Taiping prince Huang Zilong, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 復金匱、宜興、荊溪、溧陽、常州、嘉興，皆有功，累擢守備。

translations.literal: He again took Jinkui, Yixing, Jingxi, Liyang, Changzhou, and Jiaxing, all with merit, and through promotions reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He helped recapture Jinkui, Yixing, Jingxi, Liyang, Changzhou, and Jiaxing, winning credit in each, and rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 移剿捻，賊擾福山、寧海諸地，全勝分防吳家閘，潛出賊背夾擊，斃無算。

translations.literal: Shifting to suppress the Nian, when bandits harassed Fushan and Ninghai Quansheng defended at Wujia Gate, stole out behind the bandits and struck from both sides, killing beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to fight the Nian, when rebels harassed Fushan and Ninghai he held Wujia Gate, slipped behind the enemy, and struck from both sides, killing beyond count.

sentences.zh: 賊南竄，复敗之莒州、沭陽，追抵海州境，賊創亡略盡。

translations.literal: The bandits fled south; he again defeated them at Ju and Shuyang, pursued to the Haizhou border, and the bandits were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled south; he defeated them again at Ju and Shuyang and pursued to the Haizhou border until they were nearly annihilated.

sentences.zh: 贛榆六塘河之戰，斃賊尤夥。

translations.literal: At the battle of the Liutang River in Ganyu the bandits slain were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle on the Liutang River at Ganyu the enemy dead were especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，擢游擊，賞花翎。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he was promoted to raiding commander and rewarded with the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were suppressed he was promoted to raiding commander and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 張總愚竄畿南，全勝敗之安平。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region; Quansheng defeated him at Anping.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region, Quansheng defeated him at Anping.

sentences.zh: 賊偷渡滹沱河，全勝追剿偽懷王邱得才一支殆盡。

translations.literal: The bandits secretly crossed the Hutuo River; Quansheng pursued and nearly destroyed the false Huaiking Qiu Decai's division.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels stole across the Hutuo River, Quansheng pursued and nearly wiped out the division of the false Huaiking Qiu Decai.

sentences.zh: 賊趨天津，全勝冒雨急馳，繞截賊前。

translations.literal: The bandits moved toward Tianjin; Quansheng galloped through rain in haste and cut around ahead of them.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels moved toward Tianjin, Quansheng rode through rain in forced marches to cut across ahead of them.

sentences.zh: 賊回竄高唐，南走陵縣、臨邑，適黃、運漲，賊既困於水，又屢受巨創，不能軍。

translations.literal: The bandits turned back to flee to Gaotang and fled south through Ling and Linyi; just then the Yellow River and Grand Canal rose, and the bandits were trapped by water and had suffered repeated heavy blows and could not maintain an army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels doubled back toward Gaotang and fled south through Ling and Linyi. The Yellow River and Grand Canal had risen; trapped by floodwaters and battered repeatedly, they could no longer keep an army in the field.

sentences.zh: 西捻肅清，擢升參將。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified he was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were suppressed he was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 駐津沽管練軍營，率所部開濬陳家溝，抵北塘咸河百餘裡，歲溉稻田無數。

translations.literal: Garrisoning at Jingu he managed the training camp, leading his troops in opening the Chenjiagou channel more than a hundred li to the Beitang salt river, irrigating countless fields of rice each year.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed at Jingu he commanded the training camp and led his men in opening the Chenjiagou channel for more than a hundred li to the Beitang salt river, irrigating countless rice fields each year.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，以塞永定河決口功，升副將。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu, for merit in closing the Yongding River breach, he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he was promoted to vice commander for closing the breach on the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 北運河紅廟漫口，全勝率軍堵塞，詔以總兵記名。

translations.literal: When the North Canal's Hongmiao burst its banks Quansheng led troops to block it; an edict recorded him for major-general.
translations.idiomatic: When the North Canal burst at Hongmiao, Quansheng led troops to seal the breach; an edict placed him on the rolls for major-general.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，王文韶督直隸，擢充天津練軍翼長，兼帶中營砲隊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Wang Wenshao governed Zhili; Quansheng was promoted to wing commander of the Tianjin training army and also commanded the central battalion artillery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, under Wang Wenshao's governorship of Zhili, Quansheng was made wing commander of the Tianjin training army and also commanded the central battalion artillery.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，年六十，卹如例。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died at age sixty; mourning followed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died at the age of sixty; posthumous honors followed regulations.

sentences.zh: 全勝治軍四十年，與士卒同甘苦，故臨陣咸為效命；

translations.literal: Quansheng commanded troops for forty years, sharing hardship with the soldiers, so in battle all were willing to give their lives;
translations.idiomatic: Quansheng had commanded troops for forty years, sharing hardship with his men, so in battle they all fought willingly for him;

sentences.zh: 又善以寡擊眾，身經數百戰，未嘗一挫敗。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at striking many with few; through hundreds of battles he never once suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at defeating larger forces with smaller ones; through hundreds of battles he never once suffered a defeat.

sentences.zh: 鴻章恆稱之。

translations.literal: Hongzhang always praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang always spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 牛師韓，安徽渦陽人。

translations.literal: Niu Shihan, a man of Guoyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Shihan was a native of Guoyang, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父斐然，官知府，在鄉治團練。

translations.literal: His father Feiran held office as prefect and organized militia training in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feiran served as prefect and organized militia in their home district.

sentences.zh: 師韓隨父擊賊，數挫之，稱「牛家團練營」。

translations.literal: Shihan followed his father in striking bandits, defeating them many times, and they were called the Niu family militia battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Shihan fought alongside his father against bandits, routing them repeatedly, and their force was known as the Niu family militia battalion.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，投皖軍，破趙家海、檀城集，收撫各圩。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he joined the Anhui army, took Zhao Family Sea and Tanchengji, and received the surrender of various stockaded villages.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he joined the Anhui army, captured Zhao Family Sea and Tanchengji, and received the surrender of surrounding stockaded villages.

sentences.zh: 十一年，發、捻各寇竄擾睢寧。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Taiping and Nian bandits of every sort raided and harassed Suining.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Taiping and Nian rebels of every sort raided Suining.

sentences.zh: 師韓以少擊眾，克週堂，積勳至守備。

translations.literal: Shihan with few struck many, took Zhoutang, and through accumulated merit reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting against odds, Shihan captured Zhoutang and through accumulated merit rose to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，苗沛霖據鳳臺，與捻首張洛行互犄角，數百里寇寨林立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi Miao Peilin held Fengtai and with Nian chieftain Zhang Luoxing supported each other as horns; for several hundred li bandit stockades stood like forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi Miao Peilin held Fengtai and with the Nian chieftain Zhang Luoxing supported each other; for hundreds of li rebel stockades dotted the landscape.

sentences.zh: 蒙城被圍久，士卒無現糧，城幾潰。

translations.literal: Mengcheng had long been besieged; the troops had no cash grain and the city nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcheng had been besieged for a long time; the troops had no grain on hand and the city nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 英翰方牧宿州，亟赴援，而悍黨斜趨西南，將襲我後。

translations.literal: Ying Han was then governing Suzhou and hurried to relieve them, but fierce factions angled southwest intending to strike our rear.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Han, then prefect of Suzhou, hurried to relieve the city, but a strong enemy column angled southwest to strike the government rear.

sentences.zh: 適師韓率騎旅至，戰卻之，又出奇兵通運道。

translations.literal: Just then Shihan arrived with cavalry, fought them off, and also sent elite troops to open the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Shihan arrived with cavalry, drove them back, and sent elite troops to reopen the supply route.

sentences.zh: 已而英翰以鳳潁道統蒙、亳諸軍，與捻相持數月。

translations.literal: Before long Ying Han as Feng-Ying route commander commanded the Meng and Bozhou armies, contending with the Nian for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ying Han, as commander of the Feng-Ying route, directed the armies of Meng and Bozhou in a months-long standoff with the Nian.

sentences.zh: 師韓常以騎兵摧寇鋒，援師續至，復選卒潰圍會援軍，躪寇壘數十，飛彈傷額，裹創力戰，寇黨殲焉，圍解。

translations.literal: Shihan often used cavalry to break the bandit spearhead; relief troops continued to arrive; he again selected troops to break the siege and join the relief army, trampled several dozen bandit stockades, was wounded in the forehead by a flying bullet, fought on wrapped in wounds, and the bandit faction was destroyed and the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Shihan repeatedly used cavalry to shatter the enemy vanguard. As reinforcements arrived he led picked men out of the encirclement to join them, overran dozens of rebel stockades, took a bullet wound to the forehead, fought on despite his injuries, destroyed the enemy force, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 先是，英翰計擒洛行，及其子喜、義子王宛兒，夜獻僧格林沁軍，先遣師韓單騎詣大營，乞兵迎​​解，穿寇壘而過。

translations.literal: Earlier Ying Han had planned to capture Luoxing and his son Xi and adopted son Wang Wan'er, who by night were presented to Sengge Rinchen's army; he first sent Shihan alone on horseback to the great camp to beg troops to meet and escort them, passing through bandit stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ying Han had planned to capture Zhang Luoxing along with his son Xi and adopted son Wang Wan'er, who were delivered by night to Sengge Rinchen's camp. He first sent Shihan alone on horseback to the main army to request an escort, passing straight through enemy stockades.

sentences.zh: 比寇覺，馳劫之，不及，張酋竟駢誅，時師韓年甫冠也，再遷至游擊。

translations.literal: By the time the bandits realized and galloped to intercept, it was too late; the Zhang chieftain was executed in pairs; at the time Shihan was barely twenty and was twice promoted to raiding commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before the enemy could intercept him, Zhang Luoxing and his kin had been executed. Shihan was barely twenty years old and was twice promoted to raiding commander.

sentences.zh: 嗣從英翰剿發寇，戰霍山黑石渡，大敗之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed Ying Han in suppressing Taiping bandits and at Heishidu in Huoshan won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Ying Han against the Taiping and won a great victory at Heishidu in Huoshan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，陳得才、藍長春等構黨號十萬，游弋英、霍、潛、太間。

translations.literal: Before long Chen Decai, Lan Changchun, and others formed a faction numbering a hundred thousand, roaming between Ying, Huo, Qian, and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen Decai, Lan Changchun, and others formed a faction of a hundred thousand men, roaming between Yingzhou, Huoshan, Qianshan, and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 師韓請英翰剿撫兼施，不及旬日，降者踵接。

translations.literal: Shihan asked Ying Han to combine suppression and pacification; in less than ten days surrenderers came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Shihan urged Ying Han to combine military pressure with offers of surrender; within ten days defectors came in one after another.

sentences.zh: 得才窮蹙自裁，而長春猶嵎負。

translations.literal: Decai, pressed to extremity, killed himself, but Changchun still resisted stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Decai, driven to desperation, killed himself, but Lan Changchun still held out.

sentences.zh: 師韓苦戰，嬰十餘創，屹不動。

translations.literal: Shihan fought bitterly, received more than ten wounds, and stood firm without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Shihan fought on through more than ten wounds and held his ground without yielding.

sentences.zh: 旋藍逆伏誅，餘眾悉平。

translations.literal: Soon the Lan rebel was executed in ambush and the remainder were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lan Changchun was killed in an ambush and the rest were pacified.

sentences.zh: 張總愚合賴文光、任柱窺蒙、亳，圍雉河集。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu joined Lai Wenguang and Ren Zhu in watching Meng and Bozhou and besieged Zhiheji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyu joined Lai Wenguang and Ren Zhu in threatening Meng and Bozhou and besieged Zhiheji.

sentences.zh: 師韓聞警，率師直薄寇營，內外夾擊，遂解重圍，擢參將，賜號信勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Shihan heard the alarm, led troops straight to press the bandit camp, struck from within and without, and the heavy siege was lifted; he was promoted to colonel and granted the title Xinyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Shihan led his men straight at the enemy camp and attacked from inside and out, lifting the siege. He was promoted to colonel and granted the title Xinyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 六年，任柱竄山東，截之於郯城，又擊退宿遷、運河悍賊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Ren Zhu fled to Shandong; he intercepted them at Tancheng and again beat back fierce bandits at Suqian and the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Ren Zhu fled into Shandong; Shihan intercepted him at Tancheng and again drove back fierce rebels at Suqian and along the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，超擢總兵，更勇號曰達春。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he was leap-promoted to major-general with a further brave title Dachun.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were suppressed he was promoted by special leap to major-general and granted a further brave title, Dachun.

sentences.zh: 七年，西捻竄直、豫間，英翰請馳兵汴梁，入衛畿輔，檄師韓率騎旅三千會援。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the western Nian fled between Zhili and Henan; Ying Han asked to gallop troops to Bianliang and enter to guard the capital region, ordering Shihan to lead three thousand cavalry to join the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the western Nian ranged between Zhili and Henan. Ying Han requested urgent march to Kaifeng and the capital approaches, ordering Shihan to lead three thousand cavalry to the relief.

sentences.zh: 尋命駐黃河以南備守禦。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to garrison south of the Yellow River on defensive duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to garrison south of the Yellow River on defensive duty.

sentences.zh: 師韓日與豫捻鏖戰，所向輒捷，長驅山東境，復與諸軍截之恩縣。

translations.literal: Shihan battled Henan Nian day after day, victorious wherever he went; making a long drive into Shandong he again joined the armies in intercepting at En county.
translations.idiomatic: Shihan fought the Henan Nian day after day and was victorious wherever he went. Driving deep into Shandong he joined the other columns in intercepting the enemy at En county.

sentences.zh: 捻驚走，躡至鹽山、海豐，馳四晝夜抵高唐。

translations.literal: The Nian fled in alarm; he pursued to Yanshan and Haifeng, galloping four days and nights to reach Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian fled in alarm; he pursued to Yanshan and Haifeng and rode four days and nights to reach Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 捻湧至，將犯運河。

translations.literal: The Nian surged up intending to violate the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian massed and were about to strike the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 會天大風，師韓趨上風邀擊，寇大潰。

translations.literal: Just then a great wind blew; Shihan rushed to the windward side to intercept and the bandits were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind arose; Shihan took the windward position and intercepted them, and the enemy was utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified he was rewarded with a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were suppressed he was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 英翰疏稱其好謀能斷，堪勝提鎮任。

translations.literal: Ying Han memorialized that he was skilled in planning and decisive, fit for provincial commander posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Han memorialized that he was resourceful and decisive, fit for command at provincial level.

sentences.zh: 捻酋宋景詩逋誅，復以計擒僇之，晉提督，賜秩頭品。

translations.literal: The Nian chieftain Song Jingshi had escaped execution; he again captured and executed him by stratagem, was advanced to provincial military commander, and granted first-grade rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian chieftain Song Jingshi had escaped justice; Shihan captured and executed him by stratagem, was promoted to provincial military commander, and granted first-grade court rank.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，授河南歸德鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed major-general of the Guide garrison in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed major-general of the Guide garrison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，調河北鎮，遭父憂去。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to the Hebei garrison and left on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to the Hebei garrison and resigned on his father's death.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日韓構釁，授甘肅寧夏鎮，命入衛，駐軍榆關。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year conflict arose between China and Japan; he was appointed to the Ningxia garrison in Gansu, ordered to enter the capital for guard duty, and stationed troops at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year war broke out with Japan; he was appointed to the Ningxia garrison in Gansu, ordered to the capital for guard duty, and stationed his troops at Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 事定，還本官。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis ended he returned to his original post.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，河湟回蠢動，師韓赴之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Muslim rebels of the Huang and Tao rivers stirred; Shihan went to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Muslim rebels stirred in the Huang and Tao river region; Shihan went to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 次西寧，聞平戎驛被圍久，亟入。

translations.literal: Stopping at Xining he heard Pingyi post had long been besieged and entered in haste.
translations.idiomatic: At Xining he learned that Pingyi post had been besieged for a long time and entered in haste.

sentences.zh: 大峽距驛四十里，悍回數千恃險負命。

translations.literal: Great Gorge was forty li from the post; several thousand fierce Muslims relied on the terrain and fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Great Gorge lay forty li from the post; several thousand fierce Muslim fighters held the defile and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 師韓以四百人制之，血戰竟日，賊敗潰，復大峽，其小峽寇亦遁。

translations.literal: Shihan with four hundred men controlled them, fought in bloody battle all day, the bandits were defeated and fled, Great Gorge was recovered, and the bandits of the lesser gorges also fled.
translations.idiomatic: With four hundred men Shihan held them at bay, fought all day in bloody combat, routed the enemy, recovered Great Gorge, and the rebels in the lesser gorges fled as well.

sentences.zh: 旋創發，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 當其赴援時，陰雨彌旬，山迳聳巘，行帳無所用，士卒有假居旅捨者。

translations.literal: When he went to the relief, rain lasted half a month; mountain paths were steep and lofty; marching tents were useless and some soldiers lodged in travelers' inns.
translations.idiomatic: On the march to relieve the post, rain fell for half a month. The mountain paths were treacherous; tents were useless, and some men took shelter in roadside inns.

sentences.zh: 提督董福祥劾之，議奪職，師韓未及知而已疾終。

translations.literal: Provincial commander Dong Fuxiang impeached him; removal from office was debated; Shihan had not yet learned of it when he died of his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commander Dong Fuxiang impeached him and proceedings began to strip his rank. Shihan died of illness before he learned of it.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔復故官。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict restored his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 總督周馥狀其績以上，予原籍建祠。

translations.literal: Governor Zhou Fu reported his achievements upward and a temple was authorized in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhou Fu memorialized his achievements, and a memorial temple was authorized in his home district.

sentences.zh: 曹德慶，安徽廬江人。

translations.literal: Cao Deqing, a man of Lujiang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Deqing was a native of Lujiang, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 粵寇蹂皖，練團保境。

translations.literal: When Taiping bandits ravaged Anhui, militia defended the territory.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping ravaged Anhui, local militia defended the district.

sentences.zh: 嗣從官軍克柘皋、三河，被重創。

translations.literal: Thereafter following government troops he captured Zhegao and Sanhe and received grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed government troops in capturing Zhegao and Sanhe and suffered grave wounds.

sentences.zh: 改隸淮軍吳長慶麾下。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve under Wu Changqing of the Huai army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve under Wu Changqing in the Huai army.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，李鴻章督兵上海，檄德慶探賊，盡得其虛實，大破賊新橋。

translations.literal: At the change to Tongzhi, Li Hongzhang commanded troops at Shanghai and ordered Deqing to scout the bandits, learning all their strengths and weaknesses, and greatly defeated them at Xinqiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhi began, Li Hongzhang commanded at Shanghai and sent Deqing to scout the enemy. Learning their dispositions, he routed them at Xinqiao.

sentences.zh: 時總兵程學啟被圍，復從長慶疾擊之，圍解。

translations.literal: At the time major-general Cheng Xueqi was besieged; again following Changqing he struck in haste and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Major-general Cheng Xueqi was then under siege; Deqing followed Changqing in a forced march and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 自是官軍連下十餘城。

translations.literal: From then on government troops in succession took more than ten cities.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces thereafter captured more than ten cities in succession.

sentences.zh: 德慶戰常陷堅，積勳至守備。

translations.literal: Deqing often fought in the fiercest places and through accumulated merit reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Deqing repeatedly fought in the hottest engagements and rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 水陸軍規蘇州，德慶一軍為遊兵。

translations.literal: Land and water armies planned for Suzhou; Deqing's army served as mobile troops.
translations.idiomatic: As land and naval forces converged on Suzhou, Deqing's column served as mobile troops.

sentences.zh: 蘇城既下，從克無錫、金匱，移師援浙，助擊平湖、乍浦、海鹽，據寇棄城走。

translations.literal: After Suzhou fell he followed in capturing Wuxi and Jinkui, moved troops to aid Zhejiang, helped strike Pinghu, Zhapu, and Haiyan, and the bandits abandoned the cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzhou fell he helped take Wuxi and Jinkui, shifted to aid Zhejiang, and assisted in taking Pinghu, Zhapu, and Haiyan, driving the rebels from those cities.

sentences.zh: 興城寇來犯，迎擊敗之，彈貫右臂，裹創克嘉善，攻嘉興。

translations.literal: Bandits from Xingcheng came to attack; he met them and defeated them; a bullet pierced his right arm; wrapped in wounds he took Jiashan and attacked Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Xingcheng attacked; he met and defeated them. A bullet pierced his right arm, but he pressed on, took Jiashan, and assaulted Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 從劉銘傳克常州，徇下宜、荊、溧、太、嘉諸邑，晉參將。

translations.literal: Following Liu Mingchuan he captured Changzhou and swept down Yixing, Jingxi, Liyang, Taihu, and Jiaxing counties, and was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Mingchuan he captured Changzhou and swept through Yixing, Jingxi, Liyang, Taihu, and Jiaxing, and was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 再從郭松林援浙，克湖州；

translations.literal: Again following Guo Songlin he aided Zhejiang and captured Huzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Guo Songlin to aid Zhejiang and captured Huzhou;

sentences.zh: 援閩，克潭、浦。

translations.literal: aided Fujian and captured Tan and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: aided Fujian and captured Tanzhou and Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，擢總兵。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified he was promoted to major-general.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were suppressed he was promoted to major-general.

sentences.zh: 防直、東運河，銘傳困西捻黃、運間，德慶領所部橫擊之。

translations.literal: Defending the Zhili and eastern Grand Canal, when Mingchuan was hard pressed by western Nian between the Yellow River and Canal, Deqing led his troops in a lateral strike.
translations.idiomatic: While defending the Zhili and eastern Grand Canal, when Mingchuan was hard pressed by western Nian between the Yellow River and Canal, Deqing led a flanking attack.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，晉提督，賜號烈勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified he was advanced to provincial military commander and granted the title Lieyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were suppressed he was promoted to provincial military commander and granted the title Lieyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 師旋，駐守江蘇，歷揚州，徙浦口。

translations.literal: When the army returned he garrisoned Jiangsu, served at Yangzhou, and moved to Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he garrisoned Jiangsu, served at Yangzhou, and was transferred to Pukou.

sentences.zh: 會天旱，天長、盱眙鹽梟煽亂，擒其渠陳紅慶誅之，解遣脅從數万人，發粟賑饑。

translations.literal: When drought came, salt smugglers in Tianchang and Xuyi incited disorder; he captured their leader Chen Hongqing and executed him, released tens of thousands of coerced followers, and distributed grain to relieve famine.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought, salt smugglers in Tianchang and Xuyi stirred up trouble. He captured their leader Chen Hongqing and executed him, released tens of thousands of coerced followers, and distributed grain to relieve famine.

sentences.zh: 駐江陰，建議築鵝梟嘴及下關砲台。

translations.literal: Garrisoning at Jiangyin he proposed building gun platforms at Exiaozui and Xiaguan.
translations.idiomatic: While garrisoned at Jiangyin he proposed building fortifications at Exiaozui and Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，統淮揚水師，疏濬赤山湖埂，盪金陵諸河道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he commanded the Huai-Yang naval force, dredged the Chishan lake embankment, and cleared the waterways around Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he commanded the Huai-Yang naval force, dredged the Chishan lake embankment, and cleared the waterways around Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越釁起，移軍防吳淞，增築南石塘、獅子林砲台。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Franco-Vietnamese conflict arose; he moved troops to defend Wusong and added fortifications at Nanshitang and Shizilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year war broke out between France and Vietnam; he moved to defend Wusong and strengthened the forts at Nanshitang and Shizilin.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓疏薦其設防要隘，不避艱險，授狼山鎮總兵，留防如故。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan memorialized recommending his defense of strategic passes without shunning hardship; he was appointed major-general of Langshan garrison while remaining on defense as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan memorialized praising his defense of strategic passes without shirking hardship. He was appointed major-general of the Langshan garrison while continuing his defensive duties.

sentences.zh: 皖北飢，輸巨金助賑，詔旌之。

translations.literal: When north Anhui suffered famine he contributed a great sum for relief; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When north Anhui suffered famine he contributed a large sum for relief, and an edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，罷戍，赴本官。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year garrison duty ended and he went to his permanent post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his garrison assignment ended and he took up his permanent post.

sentences.zh: 時通海裡下河縱橫數百里，梟寇出沒，民苦之。

translations.literal: At the time the lower rivers of Tonghai stretched several hundred li; salt smugglers appeared and vanished and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: The lower rivers of Tonghai then stretched for hundreds of li, and salt smugglers plagued the region.

sentences.zh: 德慶盡法懲治，姦宄浸息。

translations.literal: Deqing punished to the full extent of the law and villainy gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Deqing punished offenders to the full extent of the law, and crime gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，卹如製，從祀長慶祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died; mourning followed regulations and he was granted attached worship at Changqing's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died; posthumous honors followed regulations, and he was granted attached worship at Changqing's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 馬复震，字心楷，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Ma Fuzhen, courtesy name Xinkai, was a man of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fuzhen, styled Xinkai, was a native of Tongcheng, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 曾祖宗槤、祖瑞辰、父三俊，均見儒林傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zonglian, grandfather Ruichen, and father Sanjun all appear in the Confucian biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zonglian, grandfather Ruichen, and father Sanjun all appear in the Confucian biographies.

sentences.zh: 复震年十六，襲雲騎尉。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Fuzhen inherited the yunqiwei rank.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Fuzhen inherited the yunqiwei rank.

sentences.zh: 以祖若父均死於賊，誓欲殺寇，投詩曾國籓行營。

translations.literal: Because his grandfather and father had both died at bandit hands he swore to kill the bandits and presented a poem at Zeng Guofan's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Because his grandfather and father had both been killed by rebels, he swore to destroy the enemy and presented a poem at Zeng Guofan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 國籓奇其才，遂檄令增募兵，號淮勇。

translations.literal: Guofan marveled at his talent and ordered him to recruit additional troops, styled Huai Braves.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan was struck by his talent and ordered him to raise additional troops under the name Huai Braves.

sentences.zh: 初，國籓治團練長沙，號湘勇。

translations.literal: Initially when Guofan organized militia at Changsha they were called Xiang Braves.
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan first organized militia at Changsha they were called Xiang Braves.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章募兵皖北，以淮勇繼之，然初不稱淮勇。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang recruited in north Anhui the Huai Braves followed, but at first they were not called Huai Braves.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang recruited in north Anhui, Huai forces followed, but at first they were not called Huai Braves.

sentences.zh: 淮勇之名，實自復震始。

translations.literal: The name Huai Braves in fact began with Fuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The name Huai Braves in fact began with Fuzhen.

sentences.zh: 國籓困祁門，复震扼祁門櫸根嶺。

translations.literal: When Guofan was hard pressed at Qimen, Fuzhen held Jungen Ridge at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan was besieged at Qimen, Fuzhen held Jungen Ridge.

sentences.zh: 次年，會軍禦寇石門橋。

translations.literal: The next year he joined the army in resisting bandits at Shimen Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined the army in repelling rebels at Shimen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 又從攻徽州，拔統領唐義訓於重圍。

translations.literal: Again following the attack on Huizhou he rescued commander Tang Yixun from heavy siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Huizhou he rescued commander Tang Yixun from a heavy siege.

sentences.zh: 迭克黟縣、徽郡，又大捷屯溪、岩市，以解徽州圍；

translations.literal: In succession he took Yi county and Huizhou prefecture, and won great victories at Tunxi and Yanshi, thereby lifting the Huizhou siege;
translations.idiomatic: He took Yi county and Huizhou in turn and won great victories at Tunxi and Yanshi, lifting the siege of Huizhou;

sentences.zh: 大捷孔靈，以克績溪、祁門。

translations.literal: won a great victory at Kongling and thereby captured Jixi and Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: won a great victory at Kongling and captured Jixi and Qimen.

sentences.zh: 复震性剛，不能下人，人或讒之國籓，國籓稍稍戒飭之。

translations.literal: Fuzhen's nature was stubborn and he could not defer to others; some slandered him to Guofan and Guofan gradually admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhen was headstrong and would not defer to others. Some slandered him to Guofan, who gradually admonished him.

sentences.zh: 复震頗責望國籓，謂：「不當用人言戒我，乃不我知也。」

translations.literal: Fuzhen greatly resented Guofan, saying: 'You should not use others' words to warn me—you do not understand me.'
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhen resented Guofan deeply, saying: "You should not heed others' gossip to warn me—you do not know me at all."

sentences.zh: 會左宗棠率師徵浙，調复震從攻餘杭，比戰皆捷。

translations.literal: When Zuo Zongtang led troops to campaign in Zhejiang, Fuzhen was transferred to follow in attacking Yuhang, and in battle he was always victorious.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo Zongtang marched into Zhejiang, Fuzhen was transferred to his command and took part in the assault on Yuhang, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 餘杭既克，追寇至遂安、開化、馬金。

translations.literal: After Yuhang was taken he pursued bandits to Suian, Kaihua, and Majin.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuhang fell he pursued the enemy to Suian, Kaihua, and Majin.

sentences.zh: 湖州既克，追寇至鉛山縣坊湖鎮。

translations.literal: After Huzhou was taken he pursued bandits to Fanghu town in Qianshan county.
translations.idiomatic: After Huzhou fell he pursued the enemy to Fanghu town in Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 常為諸軍選鋒，積功至副將。

translations.literal: He often served as vanguard for the various armies and through merit reached vice commander.
