translations.idiomatic: He often led the vanguard for the various columns and rose through merit to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 宗棠奏其血性過人，膽識堅定，又好學知書，請改文職，格於例，以總兵隨宗棠剿捻陝西。

translations.literal: Zongtang memorialized that his nature surpassed others, his courage and judgment were firm, and he was also fond of learning and knew books; he requested transfer to civil office but was blocked by regulations, and as major-general he followed Zongtang in suppressing Nian in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtang memorialized that his nature was exceptional, his courage and judgment steadfast, and that he was also learned and literate. He requested civil appointment, but regulations barred it; Fuzhen followed Zongtang as major-general to suppress the Nian in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 复震自初入軍，即誓死滅賊，捻平，年三十，始歸娶。

translations.literal: From his first entry into the army Fuzhen had sworn to die destroying bandits; when the Nian were pacified he was thirty and only then married.
translations.idiomatic: From his first day in the army Fuzhen had sworn to destroy the rebels or die trying. When the Nian were pacified he was thirty and only then married.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，友愛諸弟甚至。

translations.literal: He was filial to his mother and extremely affectionate toward his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his mother and deeply affectionate toward his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 生有奇姿，骯髒不平，往往至於大醉泣下，輒歌詩以自遣。

translations.literal: Born with a striking presence, unkempt and indignant at injustice, he often drank to great drunkenness and wept, then sang poetry to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had a striking presence and a rough, uncompromising temper. He often drank himself into tears and sang poetry to console himself.

sentences.zh: 海疆日益多事，朝廷圖自強，創造火輪兵船。

translations.literal: Coastal affairs grew daily more troubled; the court sought self-strengthening and created steam warships.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal affairs grew more urgent; the court pursued self-strengthening and built steam warships.

sentences.zh: 鴻章任湖廣總督，遂委复震管帶操江船，則益研求西國水師兵法。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang was governor-general of Huguang he entrusted Fuzhen to command the Caojiang fleet, and he studied Western naval tactics all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhang became governor-general of Huguang he put Fuzhen in command of the Caojiang fleet, and Fuzhen threw himself into studying Western naval tactics.

sentences.zh: 鴻章督直隸，調巡北洋，時國籓為兩江總督，仍令往來南北，且合疏薦复震沈毅有為，足勝海疆專閫。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang governed Zhili and was transferred to patrol the northern seas, at the time Guofan was governor-general of Liangjiang; Fuzhen still traveled between north and south, and together they memorialized recommending Fuzhen as steady and capable, fit for exclusive coastal command.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhang governed Zhili and patrolled the northern seas, Guofan was governor-general at Nanjing. Fuzhen still traveled between north and south, and together they recommended him as steady and capable, fit for coastal command.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，簡授陽江鎮總兵，已前卒月餘，年未四十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was appointed major-general of the Yangjiang garrison, but more than a month earlier he had died, not yet forty years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he was appointed major-general of the Yangjiang garrison, but he had died more than a month earlier, not yet forty.

sentences.zh: 於是鴻章念其積勞久，且興淮軍及海上兵船，复震皆首其事，乃奏請優恤。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hongzhang recalled his long accumulated labor and that in founding the Huai army and coastal warships Fuzhen had been first in both; he memorialized requesting generous mourning favors.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang recalled his long service and that Fuzhen had been foremost in founding the Huai army and the coastal fleet; he memorialized for generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 著有莪園詩鈔；

translations.literal: He authored E'yuan Shichao;
translations.idiomatic: He authored E'yuan Shichao;

sentences.zh: 又嘗從寇中攜父殘稿出，展轉兵間，卒請宗棠序而刊之，為馬徵君遺集。

translations.literal: he also once carried his father's surviving manuscripts out from among the bandits, and through the turns of war finally asked Zongtang to preface and publish them as Ma Zhengjun's collected works.
translations.idiomatic: he also rescued his father's surviving manuscripts from the war zone and, after many vicissitudes, secured Zongtang's preface for their publication as the collected works of Ma Zhengjun.

sentences.zh: 程文炳，字從周，安徽阜陽人。

translations.literal: Cheng Wenbing, courtesy name Congzhou, was a man of Fuyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wenbing, styled Congzhou, was a native of Fuyang, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初結鄉團自衛。

translations.literal: Initially he organized district militia for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: He first organized local militia for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 年十八，投袁甲三軍，領馬隊為選鋒，戰輒冠其曹，洊升至守備。

translations.literal: At eighteen he joined Yuan Jiasan's army, led cavalry as vanguard, in battle always led the company, and through successive promotions reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he joined Yuan Jiasan's army, led the cavalry vanguard, always topped his unit in battle, and rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從克定遠，破湖溝寇圩，補潛山營游擊。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dingyuan he broke the bandit stockade at Hugou and was made raiding commander of the Qianshan battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dingyuan, stormed the bandit stockade at Hugou, and was appointed raiding commander of the Qianshan battalion.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，率所部二千人駐蒙城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he led two thousand of his troops to garrison Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi he led two thousand men to garrison Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 會苗沛霖構捻來犯，相持八閱月，大小百十戰，數獲勝。

translations.literal: When Miao Peilin joined with Nian to attack, they contended eight months with more than a hundred large and small battles and won several times.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Peilin allied with the Nian to attack, they fought for eight months in more than a hundred engagements and won repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 已而捻酋葛小年擁眾可數万，殊死鬥，蒙圍益急，與布政使英翰內外夾擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Before long Nian chieftain Ge Xiaonian led a host of nearly tens of thousands fighting to the death; the Meng siege grew more urgent; with provincial administration commissioner Ying Han he struck from within and without and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Nian chieftain Ge Xiaonian led nearly ten thousand men in desperate fighting. The siege of Mengcheng tightened. Wenbing and Ying Han attacked from inside and out and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁軍至，誅沛霖。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen's army arrived Peilin was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengge Rinchen's army arrived, Peilin was executed.

sentences.zh: 文炳會諸軍擒小年等駢僇之，皖北始稍靖。

translations.literal: Wenbing joined the various armies in capturing Xiaonian and others, who were executed in pairs, and north Anhui began to grow somewhat calm.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing joined the other columns in capturing Xiaonian and his associates, who were executed, and north Anhui grew somewhat calm.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，任柱、賴文光復入皖。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang again entered Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang again invaded Anhui.

sentences.zh: 英翰頓雉河集，與寇相持五十餘日，餉糈不繼，兵疲饉，文炳邀擊之，軍士戰稍卻，語所部曰：「此生死呼吸之際，汝輩尚不力耶？

translations.literal: Ying Han encamped at Zhiheji and contended with bandits more than fifty days; provisions did not continue and the troops were weary and hungry; Wenbing intercepted and struck them; the soldiers' fighting slackened slightly, and he told his troops: 'This is the moment between life and death—will you still not exert yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Ying Han held Zhiheji and fought the enemy for more than fifty days. Supplies ran short and his men were exhausted. When Wenbing attacked, his troops faltered. He told them: "This is a matter of life and death—will you still not fight?

sentences.zh: 軍令在，不汝恕！」

translations.literal: Military law stands—I will not forgive you!'
translations.idiomatic: Military law stands—I will show you no mercy!"

sentences.zh: 策馬陷陣，將弁繼之，呼聲震天，寇披靡。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse into the formation, officers and men followed, shouts shook heaven, and the bandits were routed.
translations.idiomatic: He charged into the enemy ranks, his officers followed, their shouts shook the heavens, and the Nian were routed.

sentences.zh: 追戰至夜分，左臂中矛傷，裹創力戰，寇憚之。

translations.literal: Pursuing battle until nightfall his left arm was wounded by a spear; wrapped in wounds he fought on and the bandits feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fight into the night, took a spear wound to his left arm, fought on despite his injuries, and the enemy feared him.

sentences.zh: 援至，因大破虜。

translations.literal: Relief arrived and the enemy was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived and the enemy was routed.

sentences.zh: 論功，擢總兵。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to major-general.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was promoted to major-general.

sentences.zh: 五年，補貴州清江協副將，駐軍皖北。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed assistant vice commander of the Qingjiang garrison in Guizhou while garrisoning north Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed assistant vice commander of the Qingjiang garrison in Guizhou while remaining in north Anhui.

sentences.zh: 朝命英翰撫皖。

translations.literal: The court ordered Ying Han to govern Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Ying Han governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初，文炳以軍事與英翰不相能，至是稱疾不出。

translations.literal: Earlier Wenbing and Ying Han had not gotten along in military affairs; at this he claimed illness and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wenbing and Ying Han had clashed over military affairs; now he claimed illness and refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 英翰之母賢，諸將自史念祖以下均母事之。

translations.literal: Ying Han's mother was worthy; all the generals from Shi Nianzu downward treated her as mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Han's mother was a woman of virtue; the generals from Shi Nianzu downward all honored her as a mother.

sentences.zh: 英翰以母命召文炳，至則拜床下，誓捐前隙共生死。

translations.literal: Ying Han at his mother's order summoned Wenbing; when he arrived he bowed at her bedside and swore to set aside past grievances and share life and death.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's bidding Ying Han summoned Wenbing. Wenbing came, bowed at her bedside, and swore to set aside old quarrels and share life and death.

sentences.zh: 比出，即檄統前敵師幹。

translations.literal: As soon as he went out he was ordered by dispatch to command the forward army.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he left he was ordered by dispatch to command the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 是時，捻騎飄忽成流寇，李鴻章既定圈河策，文炳統皖軍萬五千人，與總兵張得勝等進擊。

translations.literal: At the time Nian cavalry were elusive and had become roving bandits; Li Hongzhang had settled on the canal encirclement strategy; Wenbing commanded fifteen thousand Anhui troops and with major-general Zhang Desheng and others pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian had become elusive cavalry raiders. Li Hongzhang had adopted the canal encirclement strategy. Wenbing commanded fifteen thousand Anhui troops and, with Zhang Desheng and others, pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 東捻勢蹙，任柱死，其黨四散，大呼文炳名求降。

translations.literal: The eastern Nian were pressed; Ren Zhu died and his faction scattered, crying Wenbing's name to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Nian were cornered. Ren Zhu was killed, his followers scattered, and they called out Wenbing's name to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鴻章逮降卒問故，僉曰：「昔皖北善後，程公以身家保鄉人。

translations.literal: Hongzhang seized surrendered soldiers to ask the reason; all said: 'In former days in north Anhui's recovery, Master Cheng with his person and family guaranteed the people of the district.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang questioned the prisoners. They all said: "In the old days, when north Anhui was being pacified, Master Cheng pledged his person and family for the people of the region.

sentences.zh: 今我輩窮而乞憐，必能拯我。」

translations.literal: Now we are destitute and beg for mercy—he will surely save us.'
translations.idiomatic: Now we are desperate and begging for mercy—he will surely save us."

sentences.zh: 其信義孚人如此。

translations.literal: His trust and righteousness won people thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the faith his integrity inspired.

sentences.zh: 英翰上其功，擢提督。

translations.literal: Ying Han reported his merit and he was promoted to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Han reported his merit and he was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，西捻張總愚北犯，詔文炳率師入直會剿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the western Nian Zhang Zongyu invaded north; an edict ordered Wenbing to lead troops into Zhili to join the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhang Zongyu's western Nian pushed north; an edict ordered Wenbing to lead troops into Zhili for the joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，敗之滹沱河。

translations.literal: After more than a year he defeated them at the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he defeated them at the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 各軍至，捻狂奔，爭先渡河，棄騾馬貲糧河干。

translations.literal: When the various armies arrived the Nian fled wildly, competing to cross the river first, abandoning mules, horses, goods, and grain on the dry riverbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies closed in the Nian fled wildly, racing to cross the river and abandoning pack animals, goods, and grain on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 文炳下令軍中曰：「速濟追賊，敢取物者斬！」

translations.literal: Wenbing ordered the army: 'Cross quickly and pursue the bandits—whoever takes booty will be beheaded!'
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing ordered his men: "Cross quickly and pursue the enemy—anyone who seizes loot will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 於是皖軍先渡，躡賊而南，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Anhui army crossed first, pursued the bandits south, and beheaded beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The Anhui troops crossed first, pursued south, and killed the enemy in numbers beyond count.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，賞黃馬褂，還駐亳。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified he was rewarded with a yellow jacket and returned to garrison at Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were suppressed he was awarded a yellow riding jacket and returned to garrison Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授江西九江鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed major-general of the Jiujiang garrison in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed major-general of the Jiujiang garrison in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，移疾去。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年，秦、晉大饑，捐巨貲佐袁保恆辦賑濟，民獲甦。

translations.literal: The next year Shaanxi and Shanxi suffered great famine; he donated a great sum to assist Yuan Baoheng in relief work and the people were revived.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shaanxi and Shanxi suffered severe famine. He donated a large sum to assist Yuan Baoheng's relief work, and the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 五年，起署壽春鎮，旋補官南贛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled to act at the Shouchun garrison and soon appointed to permanent office at Nan'gan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to act at the Shouchun garrison and soon received permanent appointment at Nan'gan.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢湖北提督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 綠營廢弛久，文炳既受事，實行加餉抽練法，軍容一振。

translations.literal: The Green Standard troops had long been lax; once Wenbing took office he actually implemented the methods of added pay and selected drilling, and military bearing was revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Green Standard army had long been neglected. Once Wenbing took office he implemented supplemental pay and selective drilling, and the troops' bearing was restored.

sentences.zh: 蒞官十載，遭本生繼母憂，終喪。

translations.literal: He held office ten years, suffered mourning for his stepmother by birth, and completed the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for ten years, observed mourning for his stepmother, and completed the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 會中日戰事起，詔趣赴京。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese war arose an edict urgently ordered him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out with Japan an edict urgently summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至則命統皖軍駐守張家灣，尋授福建提督。

translations.literal: On arrival he was ordered to command Anhui troops garrisoning Zhangjiawan and soon appointed provincial military commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was ordered to command Anhui troops at Zhangjiawan and was soon appointed provincial military commander of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，入覲，假歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he attended court audience and took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he attended court and then took leave.

sentences.zh: 明年，拳亂作，詔福建、江南、浙江、安徽、江西勤王軍受節度，赴彰、衛、懷備守禦。

translations.literal: The next year the Boxer disturbance arose; edicts placed the loyalist armies of Fujian, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Anhui, and Jiangxi under unified command to go to Zhang, Wei, and Huai for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Boxer uprising broke out. Edicts placed the loyalist forces of Fujian, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Anhui, and Jiangxi under unified command for defense along the Zhang, Wei, and Huai routes.

sentences.zh: 又明年，提督長江水師，目睹船械窳敝，乃牒商劉坤一、張之洞改用快槍；

translations.literal: The next year he was made provincial commander of the Yangtze naval force; seeing ships and weapons worn and inferior, he memorialized Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong to adopt quick-firing rifles;
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took command of the Yangtze naval force. Seeing the ships and arms were worn out, he petitioned Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong to adopt quick-firing rifles;

sentences.zh: 調師船二百，編為游擊備策應。

translations.literal: two hundred training ships were reorganized as raiding forces for contingency response.
translations.idiomatic: two hundred training ships were reorganized as a mobile reserve.

sentences.zh: 又以師船舊砲不能擊遠，與緣江各省籌易快砲，增餉益師，軍威始壯。

translations.literal: Because the training ships' old cannon could not strike at distance, with provinces along the river he planned to exchange for quick-firing guns, increased pay and strengthened troops, and military prestige began to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Because the old guns on the training ships lacked range, he worked with the river provinces to obtain quick-firing artillery, increased pay, and expanded the force until its prestige was restored.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，卒，年七十有七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he died at age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuantong he died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔疆閫諸臣條陳時政，文炳洞見新軍癥結，具疏未上。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered frontier commanders to memorialize on current policy; Wenbing clearly saw the maladies of the new army and drafted a memorial but had not yet submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the throne had ordered frontier commanders to submit policy recommendations. Wenbing had clearly identified the ailments of the new army and drafted a memorial but had not yet submitted it.

sentences.zh: 俄病篤，命繕入遺摺中，分編兵籍、節餉糈、增額缺、造器械、變操法五事。

translations.literal: Soon he fell gravely ill and ordered it copied into his final memorial, dividing into five matters: reorganizing military registers, economizing provisions, increasing authorized posts, manufacturing weapons, and changing drill methods.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell gravely ill and ordered the draft incorporated into his deathbed memorial in five sections: reorganizing military registers, economizing supplies, increasing authorized posts, manufacturing weapons, and reforming drill methods.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其老成謀國，下所司行。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his seasoned counsel for the state and ordered the relevant offices to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his seasoned counsel for the state and ordered the relevant offices to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒卹，予本籍及立功省分建祠，諡壯勤。

translations.literal: An excellent edict granted generous mourning favors, ordered temples built in his home district and provinces where he had won merit, and posthumous title Zhuangqin.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict granted generous posthumous honors, authorized temples in his home district and in provinces where he had earned merit, and gave him the posthumous title Zhuangqin.

sentences.zh: 方耀，字照軒，廣東普寧人。

translations.literal: Fang Yao, courtesy name Zhaoxuan, was a man of Puning in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yao, styled Zhaoxuan, was a native of Puning, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，隨其父原治鄉團，所部多悍勇。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng he followed his father in organizing district militia; his troops were mostly fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he followed his father in organizing local militia; his men were mostly fierce fighters.

sentences.zh: 嗣投官軍，徵土匪有功，補把總。

translations.literal: Thereafter he joined government troops, campaigned against local bandits with merit, and was made warrant officer.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined government forces, fought local bandits with distinction, and was appointed warrant officer.

sentences.zh: 自是連克清遠、廣寧、德慶，截擊連州竄匪。

translations.literal: From then on he in succession captured Qingyuan, Guangning, and Deqing and intercepted bandits fleeing from Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Qingyuan, Guangning, and Deqing in succession and intercepted bandits fleeing from Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 總督黃宗漢疏薦謀勇冠軍，敘都司，賜號展勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Governor Huang Zonghan memorialized recommending him as foremost in stratagem and courage; he was ranked company commander and granted the title Zhanyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Huang Zonghan memorialized him as foremost in courage and strategy. He was ranked company commander and granted the title Zhanyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 九年，發寇陳四虎侵廣寧，土匪四應。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Taiping bandit Chen Sihu invaded Guangning and local bandits responded on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Taiping rebel Chen Sihu invaded Guangning and local bandits rose on every side.

sentences.zh: 耀入自英德，會水師抵三峽，沉賊船，水路始通。

translations.literal: Yao entered from Yingde; the naval force reached Sanxia and sank bandit boats; the water route was then open.
translations.idiomatic: Yao advanced from Yingde; the naval force reached Sanxia and sank rebel boats, reopening the water route.

sentences.zh: 進解陽山圍，擊退婆迳、黃陂各匪，匪奔韶州，復大破之。

translations.literal: Advancing he relieved the Yangshan siege, struck and drove off bandits at Pojing and Huangpi; the bandits fled to Shaozhou and he again defeated them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved the siege of Yangshan, drove off bandits at Pojing and Huangpi, pursued them to Shaozhou, and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 十年，從克仁化、南雄。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed in capturing Renhua and Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he took part in capturing Renhua and Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 總督勞崇光倚以破賊，令援贛，連下安遠、平遠。

translations.literal: Governor Lao Chongguang relied on him to break bandits and ordered him to aid Gan, in succession taking Anyuan and Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lao Chongguang relied on him to break the rebels and sent him to aid Jiangxi, capturing Anyuan and Pingyuan in succession.

sentences.zh: 十一年，援閩疆，下武平、永定。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he aided the Fujian frontier and took Wuping and Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he aided the Fujian frontier and captured Wuping and Yongding.

sentences.zh: 時偽興王陳金缸陷信宜，數犯高州。

translations.literal: At the time the false Xingwang Chen Jingang had taken Xinyi and repeatedly invaded Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The false Xingwang Chen Jingang had seized Xinyi and repeatedly threatened Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 耀還軍助擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Yao returned his army to assist in the attack and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yao brought his troops back to assist and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，肇、羅寇氛熾，客匪眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi bandit atmosphere in Zhao and Luo was fierce; guest bandits numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi rebellion flared in Zhaoqing and Luoding; guest bandits numbered more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 耀與副將卓興以所部八千人夾擊之，迭破巨壘，焚其屯糧。

translations.literal: Yao with vice commander Zhuo Xing used their eight thousand men in a pincer attack, in succession breaking great fortresses and burning their stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and vice commander Zhuo Xing led eight thousand men in a pincer attack, stormed major fortresses, and burned their grain stores.

sentences.zh: 其黨鄭金斬金缸以降，鄭金即鄭紹忠也。

translations.literal: His faction Zheng Jin beheaded Jingang to surrender; Zheng Jin was Zheng Shaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Zheng Jin beheaded Jingang and surrendered; Zheng Jin was Zheng Shaozhong.

sentences.zh: 高州平，晉副將。

translations.literal: When Gaozhou was pacified he was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozhou was pacified he was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，赴平遠八尺墟，坐縣城失守、進兵遲誤，暫褫職。

translations.literal: In the third year he went to the Bachi market at Pingyuan; because the county city had been lost and troop advance was delayed he was temporarily stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went to Bachi market in Pingyuan. Because the county seat had fallen and his advance was delayed, he was temporarily stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 時發寇丁太陽分據武平，耀自平遠進逼，奮擊退之。

translations.literal: At the time Taiping bandit Ding Taiyang held Wuping in divided occupation; Yao advanced from Pingyuan pressing close and struck fiercely to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebel Ding Taiyang held Wuping. Yao advanced from Pingyuan, pressed hard, and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 又設伏誘敵，乘勝徑斫賊營，大潰，城賊亦驚走，遂克武平；

translations.literal: He also set an ambush to lure the enemy, took advantage of victory to cut straight into the bandit camp, and won a great rout; the city bandits also fled in alarm and Wuping was taken;
translations.idiomatic: He set an ambush, lured the enemy in, and stormed their camp in a rout. The garrison fled in alarm and Wuping fell;

sentences.zh: 而丁賊猶據永定，負固不下，耀進圍之，诇知賊將赴金砂，隱卒以待。

translations.literal: but Ding's bandits still held Yongding and stubbornly would not yield; Yao advanced to besiege them, learned the bandit generals were going to Jinsha, and hid troops to wait.
translations.idiomatic: but Ding's men still held Yongding. Yao besieged the city, learned the rebel generals were bound for Jinsha, and hid troops to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 賊至，伏起，賊返奔，追襲之，奪城外砲樓土壘，俯瞰城中，日夜下襲，賊屍山積，啟東門遁，復故官。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived the ambush rose; bandits turned and fled; he pursued and struck, seized outer gun towers and earthworks overlooking the city, raided day and night, bandit corpses piled like mountains, they opened the east gate and fled, and his former office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came the ambush struck. They fled; he pursued, seized outer towers and earthworks overlooking the city, attacked day and night until corpses piled like hills, and the enemy opened the east gate and fled. His rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 四年，偽康王汪海洋竄大埔，耀還軍扼守，遇偽侍王李世賢，血戰三晝夜，以少擊眾，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the false Kangwang Wang Haiyang fled to Dapu; Yao returned his army to hold the line, met the false Shiwang Li Shixian, fought in bloody battle three days and nights, with few struck many, and won a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the false Kangwang Wang Haiyang fled to Dapu. Yao returned to block him, met the false Shiwang Li Shixian, and fought for three days and nights against odds, routing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 復與紹忠會師入閩，連克平和、詔安、長樂、鎮平，而餘匪嘯聚和平者勢猶盛。

translations.literal: Again joining Shaozhong's army he entered Fujian and in succession took Pinghe, Zhao'an, Changle, and Zhenping, while remaining bandits gathered at Pinghe still had strong force.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Shaozhong he entered Fujian and captured Pinghe, Zhao'an, Changle, and Zhenping, though rebels still massed at Pinghe in strength.

sentences.zh: 耀以無備，再褫職。

translations.literal: Yao because he was unprepared was again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been unprepared, Yao was again stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 旋收嘉應，复官。

translations.literal: Soon Jiaying was recovered and his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiaying was recovered and his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 七年，授南韶連鎮總兵，調署潮州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed major-general of the Nanshao-Lian garrison and transferred to act at Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed major-general of the Nanshao-Lian garrison and transferred to act at Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 潮俗故悍，械鬥奪敓以為常，甚且負嵎築寨，拒兵抗糧。

translations.literal: Chaozhou custom was formerly fierce; armed fights and robbery were commonplace, and some even relied on terrain to build stockades, resisting troops and refusing grain levies.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhou had long been a violent place where armed feuds and robbery were commonplace; some built stockades on difficult ground and resisted troops and tax collection.

sentences.zh: 耀以為積匪不除，民患不息，乃創為選舉清鄉法，先辦陸豐鬥案，明正其罪。

translations.literal: Yao believed that accumulated bandits not eliminated meant the people's suffering would not cease; he therefore created the method of elected village pacification, first handling the Lufeng feud cases and clearly establishing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yao believed that until entrenched banditry was uprooted the people would never know peace. He devised an elected village pacification system, beginning with the Lufeng feud cases.

sentences.zh: 潮人始知有官法。

translations.literal: The people of Chaozhou first learned there was government law.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chaozhou learned for the first time that government law existed.

sentences.zh: 陳獨目結會戕官，謝奉章恃險擅命，並捕治之，潮民遂安堵。

translations.literal: Chen Dumu formed a society and killed officials; Xie Fengzhang relied on terrain and acted on his own authority; both were captured and punished, and the people of Chaozhou then lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dumu formed a secret society and murdered officials; Xie Fengzhang held defensible ground and defied authority. Both were captured and punished, and Chaozhou grew calm.

sentences.zh: 暇輒釐佔產，徵逋賦，丈沙田，潮稅歲增鉅萬。

translations.literal: In leisure he rectified seized property, collected overdue taxes, and measured sand fields; Chaozhou revenue increased by tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: In quieter moments he audited seized property, collected overdue taxes, and surveyed sand fields, increasing Chaozhou's revenue by tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 又禦水患以保農田，建書院以育俊秀，士民頌之。

translations.literal: He also defended against flood harm to protect farmland and built academies to nurture talented youths; scholars and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He also built flood defenses to protect farmland and founded academies to educate talented youths; scholars and commoners praised him.

sentences.zh: 總督瑞麟狀其績以上，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Governor Ruilin reported his achievements upward and he was rewarded with a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ruilin memorialized his achievements and he was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，調署陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to act as land-force provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to act as land-force provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，還本官，治潮州、南澳、碣石軍事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he returned to his permanent post, managing military affairs at Chaozhou, Nan'ao, and Jieshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to his permanent post, overseeing military affairs at Chaozhou, Nan'ao, and Jieshi.

sentences.zh: 九年，法越構兵，充海防全軍翼長，改署水師提督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year France and Vietnam went to war; he served as wing commander of the full coastal defense army and was transferred to act as naval provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year war broke out between France and Vietnam. He served as wing commander of the coastal defense army and was transferred to act as naval provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 越二年，實授。

translations.literal: Two years later he received permanent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he received permanent appointment.

sentences.zh: 嘗率師出搗盜穴，廣、惠安謐。

translations.literal: He once led troops out to storm bandit lairs and Guangzhou and Huizhou grew tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He once led troops to storm bandit lairs, and Guangzhou and Huizhou grew tranquil.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; mourning followed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died; posthumous honors followed regulations.

sentences.zh: 耀身矯捷，履山險若平地，眼有異光，暮夜擊槍靡弗中，以故粵中諸匪咸憚之。

translations.literal: Yao's body was agile; he tread mountain dangers like level ground; his eyes had strange light; shooting guns at night he never missed; therefore all bandits in Guangdong feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was agile as a cat and crossed mountain trails as if on level ground. His eyes had an uncanny gleam, and he never missed a night shot. Every bandit in Guangdong feared him.

sentences.zh: 紹忠，籍三水。

translations.literal: Shaozhong, registered in Sanshui.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhong was registered in Sanshui.

sentences.zh: 始隨金缸為寇，既自贖，提督昆壽許領其眾為一營，號安勇。

translations.literal: Initially he followed Jingang as a bandit; after he redeemed himself provincial commander Kunshou permitted him to lead his followers as one battalion, styled Anyong.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed Jingang as a rebel. After submitting, provincial commander Kunshou allowed him to lead his followers as a battalion called Anyong.

sentences.zh: 克廣西岑溪，賞都司銜，始更名。

translations.literal: Capturing Cenxi in Guangxi he was rewarded with company commander rank and then changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing Cenxi in Guangxi he was awarded company commander rank and then took his new name.

sentences.zh: 永定、大埔之役，與有功。

translations.literal: In the Yongding and Dapu campaigns he shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: He shared credit in the Yongding and Dapu campaigns.

sentences.zh: 數遷至副將，權羅定協。

translations.literal: Through several promotions he reached vice commander and acted at the Luoding garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Through several promotions he reached vice commander and acted at the Luoding garrison.

sentences.zh: 寇據嘉應，其黨譚光明等殊死戰。

translations.literal: Bandits held Jiaying; their faction Tan Guangming and others fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Jiaying; their leader Tan Guangming and others fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 紹忠扼守長沙墟，寇至，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shaozhong held Changshaxu; when bandits came he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhong held Changshaxu; when the enemy came he attacked and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 城寇悉眾出，並力追擊，擒渠率，城拔。

translations.literal: The city bandits all came out in full force; he pursued with combined strength, captured leaders, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison came out in full force; he pursued with combined strength, captured the leaders, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 以次徵肇慶、思平諸匪，賜號敢勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In succession he campaigned against Zhaoqing, Xiping, and other bandits and was granted the title Ganyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in succession against Zhaoqing, Xiping, and other bandits and was granted the title Ganyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 平五坑客匪，更勇號額騰伊。

translations.literal: Pacifying the Wukeng guest bandits he received a further brave title Etengyi.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the Wukeng guest bandits he received a further brave title, Etengyi.

sentences.zh: 自是察匪所向，捕之。

translations.literal: From then on he observed where bandits were headed and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he tracked where the bandits went and captured them.

sentences.zh: 不二年，擢提督，補潮州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In less than two years he was promoted to provincial military commander and appointed major-general of the Chaozhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he was promoted to provincial military commander and appointed to the Chaozhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，搜治欽州、靈山積匪，晉秩頭品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he searched out and suppressed accumulated bandits in Qinzhou and Lingshan and was given first-grade rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he suppressed entrenched bandits in Qinzhou and Lingshan and was awarded first-grade court rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，攻克瓊州、儋臨，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he captured Qiongzhou and Danlin and was rewarded with a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he captured Qiongzhou and Danlin and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 十年，權陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he acted as land-force provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he acted as land-force provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 粵故多匪，紹忠頗善治之。

translations.literal: Guangdong had always had many bandits; Shaozhong was quite skilled in governing them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had always been plagued by bandits, and Shaozhong was especially skilled at suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 攻剿遍粵境，轉戰閩、桂，匪為斂跡。

translations.literal: Campaigning throughout Guangdong and fighting in Fujian and Guangxi, bandits fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned throughout Guangdong and fought in Fujian and Guangxi until banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授湖南提督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十七年，還綜廣東水師。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned to overall command of Guangdong naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he returned to overall command of the Guangdong naval forces.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was given ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 越二年，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: Two years later he died; mourning followed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died; posthumous honors followed regulations.

sentences.zh: 鄧安邦，廣東東莞人。

translations.literal: Deng Anbang, a man of Dongguan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Anbang was a native of Dongguan, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 以勇目積功至守備。

translations.literal: As a brave subordinate through accumulated merit he reached garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a brave fighter he rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，從耀等克武平。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he followed Yao and others in capturing Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongzhi he followed Yao and others in capturing Wuping.

sentences.zh: 四年，汪海洋陷鎮平，圍平遠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wang Haiyang took Zhenping and besieged Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Haiyang seized Zhenping and besieged Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 安邦赴援，抵城下，飢疲甚，雜食薯芋，卒解城圍。

translations.literal: Anbang went to the relief, reached below the city wall, was extremely hungry and weary, ate taro and yams mixed together, and finally lifted the city siege.
translations.idiomatic: Anbang marched to relieve the city, arrived exhausted and starving, subsisted on taro and yams, and finally lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 再敗賊大柘、超竹。

translations.literal: Again he defeated bandits at Dazhe and Chaozhu.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the enemy at Dazhe and Chaozhu.

sentences.zh: 嘉應陷，與諸軍截殲之，晉游擊，賜號銳勇巴圖魯，遷參將。

translations.literal: When Jiaying fell he with the various armies intercepted and destroyed them; he was promoted to raiding commander, granted the title Ruiyong Batulu, and transferred to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaying fell he joined the other columns in destroying the enemy, was promoted to raiding commander, granted the title Ruiyong Batulu, and transferred to colonel.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，補清遠營游擊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was appointed raiding commander of the Qingyuan battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he was appointed raiding commander of the Qingyuan battalion.

sentences.zh: 明年，匪首歐就起襲據佛岡廳，安邦約紹忠內外合攻，復其城，獲就起，置之法。

translations.literal: The next year bandit chief Ou Jiuqi rose and seized Fogang subprefecture; Anbang arranged with Shaozhong for inner and outer combined attack, recovered the city, captured Jiuqi, and punished him by law.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the bandit chief Ou Jiuqi seized Fogang. Anbang coordinated with Shaozhong for a combined assault, recovered the city, captured Jiuqi, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授湖州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed major-general of the Huzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed major-general of the Huzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自發、捻起，各省興團練，淮、皖為盛，實淮勇之始也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From the rise of Taiping and Nian, every province raised militia training; Huai and Wan were most flourishing—this was in fact the beginning of Huai Braves.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: From the rise of the Taiping and Nian rebellions, every province raised militia; Huai and Wan were foremost—this was the true beginning of the Huai Braves.

sentences.zh: 東才以下諸人，初皆起鄉團，其後或隸豫軍，或隸淮軍，皆先後著戰績，為時所稱。

translations.literal: The men from Dongcai downward all initially rose from district militia; thereafter some served the Henan army, some the Huai army, all in time winning battle merit and praised by their age.
translations.idiomatic: From Dongcai onward these men all began in local militia; some later joined the Henan army, others the Huai army, and all in time won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 方耀以粵團歸官軍，善戰兼謀勇，尤善治盜，民多感頌，茲故並著之。

translations.literal: Fang Yao with Guangdong militia joined government troops, skilled in battle and also in stratagem and courage, especially skilled in governing bandits; the people widely praised him—therefore he is recorded here together.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yao brought Guangdong militia into government service, combining fighting skill with strategy and courage, and was especially adept at suppressing bandits. The people praised him widely—hence he is recorded here with the others.
